text: Hypothesis: Idea-graph grounding improves autonomous long-horizon software delivery versus a stateless baseline
description: Run a controlled benchmark on a fixed set of representative repository tasks. Compare (A) the wrapped agent using Aimparency context, prioritization, durable memory, reflection, and recovery with (B) the same model/tool budget using only the task prompt and repository. Pre-register tasks and scoring. Measure verified task completion, human interventions, wall-clock time, token/tool cost, recovery from injected failure, and policy violations. Pass only if the graph-grounded condition improves verified completion or materially reduces intervention without worse safety. Preserve prompts, run records, commits, tests, and negative results.

supportingConnections.hypothesis: Pre-registers and analyzes the controlled comparison required by the parent hypothesis.
Enables collection of controlled paired empirical evidence.
Supplies the missing empirical evidence for the graph-grounding hypothesis.
Builds on the valid null v1 experiment and its observed ceiling effect.

status.comment: Felix review triage 2026-11-01: the pre-registered hypothesis did not hold. v1 and calibrated v3 matched benchmarks were valid nulls (equal completion, zero interventions, no qualifying efficiency gain); v2 was invalid. Follow-up question lives in 926212fd (multi-session benchmark).

valueRationale: A controlled baseline is necessary to distinguish genuine autonomy gains from activity, anecdotes, or model capability alone.
